title: Coptic Reference dictionary entry
description: One merged entry from CCL + CDO + Kaikki + corpus counts. Closed: additionalProperties is false, so an emitter that invents a field fails the build rather than silently shipping it. attributions[] is the CC BY-SA §3(b) declaration of what we changed and whose work it came from.

id.description: TLA lemma id when available (e.g. C5047); otherwise a stable hash of (norm_key|pos).

display.description: As presented. Keeps diacritics. The <norm_key> is what we join and sort on; never display the canonical form in place of the diplomatic one.

norm_key.description: NFC + combining marks stripped + case folded. THE JOIN KEY. Merging, dedup and lookup all use this, never raw orthography - see the enclitic case <norm orig='ⲥ' lemma='ⲛⲧⲟⲥ'>.

translit.description: Transliteration per scheme. Values are conventions, so a bad one is a correctness bug, not a preference.

dialects.description: Union across sources; never overwrite. A lemma legitimately attested in both carries both. S=Sahidic B=Bohairic N=undetermined A=Assiutic Ak=Akhmimic F=Fayumic L/M/P/V/W are further CCL codes, preserved verbatim because this project has not established their expansions and a wrong expansion is worse than an unexpanded one. CORRECTED Session 3: this enum previously read [B, S, N, S/B, B/S] and excluded eight values the real CCL v1.2-2020 actually uses (S 9418, B 2221, A 822, M 747, L 725, F 617, V 146, Ak 93, W 57, P 7). An entry with no dialect evidence from any source carries [N], which is what N means. See DECISIONS.md S3-D2.

pos.description: Controlled part-of-speech vocabulary, normalised at merge time by tools/pos.py. The enum is the same 21-value set, duplicated here deliberately: the schema is what dry_run --real and any third-party consumer validate against, so it must be self-contained.

glosses.description: minItems 1 is a licence gate, not a content preference: every entry must carry at least one gloss with an attribution.

etymology.description: Kaikki's etymology prose chains (Greek / Demotic / Egyptian) are the best readable form available and are NOT reproduced by CCL, so this is a primary use for Kaikki.

source.description: DELIBERATELY NARROWER than ALLOWED_SOURCES: an etymology comes from a lexicon, not from a corpus or treebank, so the corpus ids are not offered here. Must remain a subset of ALLOWED_SOURCES in tools/validate/nc_guard.py; tools/tests/test_guards.py enforces that.

work_slug.description: Key into data/dist/corpus/manifest.json and public/data/corpus/. Needed to locate the tokens that back this ref; a urn alone does not identify a local file.

work_title.description: Display title. Kept beside the slug so a reader-facing page needs no lookup.

occurrences.description: Token count in this work. VERIFIED against the tarball by tools/tests/test_full_roundtrip.py ::test_corpus_ref_counts_match_the_tarball_exactly — a corpus_ref whose count disagrees with the corpus fails the build. Added Session 4 (D6): the first corpus_refs bake failed here because this object was closed to {urn, freq_per_10k, lemma_rank}, and the round-trip needs a work key and a checked count. See DECISIONS.md S4-D2.

forms.description: Attested inflected forms. Drives the reverse-lookup index so a learner can click any token and land on its lemma.

kind.description: romanization = a transliteration of the headword, NOT an inflection. Showing one as the other is a visible correctness bug: `xalkin` is not an inflected form of `\u2c e7\u2c81\u2d15\u2c93\u2c9b`. Kaikki tags these with tags=[romanization] vs tags=[plural] and the distinction is carried through from tools/parse/kaikki.py.

media.description: images: PD historical illustration, commissioned iconography under clear terms, or non-figurative ornament ONLY. AI-generated depictions of Christ, the Theotokos, saints, angels or liturgical scenes are PROHIBITED - see GOVERNANCE.md and the image content policy.

source_url.description: Mandatory for PD imagery. Where it came from is part of the rights.

reviewer.description: Church-bloc reviewer who approved this image. Required before production.

synthetic.description: Only ever true for non-figurative decorative imagery.

sources.description: Which upstream sources contributed. Every id here must appear in records.csv and in ALLOWED_SOURCES.

attributions.description: CC BY-SA 4.0 §3(b) requires indicating modifications. minItems 1 means every entry declares where each field came from AND what we did to it. 'changes' uses a controlled vocabulary so it can be aggregated - that is how we can report, in total, how much of this dictionary is verbatim. The PROJECT AUTHOR NEVER APPEARS HERE; his credit is project-level. See GOVERNANCE.md §Attribution.

field.description: Session 6 D2: 'pos' was added because the merge now normalises part-of-speech to the controlled vocabulary in tools/pos.py, and that IS a change to a field. Declaring it here is what makes the change attributable under CC BY-SA 3(b) instead of invisible.

source.description: FREE STRING, per v4 §8.2, and this is load-bearing. An attribution may cite a per-document or per-sub-source label ('Coptic Scriptorium _TT'), not only an id. The consequence is that nc_guard.py — not this schema — is the primary control on attribution provenance, because nothing here constrains the value. Emit ids from ALLOWED_SOURCES (plus MERGE) so the guard can judge them. See DECISIONS.md S2-B3.

record_ids.description: Per-source record ids, so any gloss can be traced to the exact upstream entry.

collation_hash.description: The sort alphabet in force when this entry was emitted. See tools/collate.py.
